headline: Multiomic brain profiling links 3D genome, isoform usage and cortical folding genetics
label: Brain Multiomics And Representation Learning
summary: Single-cell and single-molecule brain profiling now resolves genome architecture, isoform usage and cortical morphology at cell and individual level.
synthesis: The dominant thread is high-resolution, multimodal profiling of primate and human brain, with learned representations extracting structure from complex data. Fullscope-seq maps cell-type and layer-specific isoform usage across macaque brain regions at single-molecule resolution. Single-cell GAGE-seq jointly captures 3D chromatin and gene expression in Alzheimer's postmortem brain, and Hicformer links 3D genome features to these profiles. SynAPSeg applies deep learning to synaptic puncta segmentation in hippocampal tissue, with an open dataset. A self-supervised preprint compares 56 cortical folding representations with classical sulcal morphometry via multivariate GWAS in 35,940 UK Biobank participants. What is new is that genome architecture, isoform usage and cortical morphology are each resolved at cell or individual level and tied to molecular or genetic readouts.
